structured_output.summary: Phase 8 is substantively strong and unusually honest. I independently re-derived the gate's command set from `tools/check_phase.py` (phase 1→8 chain yields exactly 77 commands) and confirmed `docs/checks/phase-08.json` records all 77 with `exit_code: 0`, `source_unchanged: true`, and `source_sha256: e5903a90…` matching the reviewed source. The parity matrix is machine-enforced and fail-closed: `tools/qualification.py` requires exactly 448 frozen operations, 3,820 implemented export capabilities, hash-bound source/test bindings, no constructor or family promotion, and zero unexplained gaps (`operations 448, implemented 448, contractVerified 448, unexplainedGaps 0`). Live evidence is conservative and sanitized: 17 verified methods, 3×403 permission prerequisites, 2×400 service-contract rejections with the cause explicitly unestablished and an SDK defect explicitly not excluded, cleanup `not_needed` because nothing was created. Platform labels are honest (musl native execution vs four compile-only targets with transports excluded), package checks are real (archive extraction with member-safety limits, packaged unit tests, doctests, example compilation, and an external 3,820-probe consumer), the dependency audit is fresh (RustSec HEAD `64f92cdc`, 0 vulnerabilities, 206 licensed packages), and `unsafe_code = "forbid"` is enforced workspace-wide. The CI-bootstrap correction itself is well handled: the exit-127 failure was reproduced, a new guard (`test_every_job_bootstraps_rust_before_running_commands`) fails on the pre-fix workflow and passes on the corrected one, and I verified from the cached pinned manifest that `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@683b588c` does install rustup when absent and exports Cargo on `$GITHUB_PATH`, so the fix genuinely addresses the reported failure mode. What holds this below the threshold is not functionality but delivery documentation accuracy, which is itself a phase-8 deliverable: the correction added two new pinned third-party actions and left `docs/CI.md` — the designated CI evidence document — describing the pre-correction world, including a now-false "only two third-party actions" enumeration, a now-false claim that the workflow does not change the runner default toolchain, and stale rustup/Python prerequisites. Secondarily, the phase-8 delivery bookkeeping still presents the superseded commit's push and clean-archive proof as the current delivery state.

findings.description: docs/CI.md was not updated for the change under review and now materially misdescribes the corrected workflow's third-party action surface. It states "Only two third-party actions are used, pinned to commits" and its table (lines 26-29) lists only actions/checkout and actions/setup-node. The corrected .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml uses four distinct actions across 11 `uses:` references, including actions/setup-python (ci.yml:35, 92, 126) and dtolnay/rust-toolchain (ci.yml:39, 44, 87, 121) — the latter being precisely the component that downloads and executes https://sh.rustup.rs on the runner (verified in .local/ci-bootstrap-2026-10-17/rust-toolchain.action.yml:63-70). tools/test_ci.py:46-52 correctly asserts all four identities, so the machine guard and the delivery document disagree, and the document understates the supply-chain trust surface added by this correction. Unlike the pre-existing pins, the dtolnay pin has no inline tag/version comment and no recorded tag-to-commit binding anywhere (docs/checks/phase-08-ci-actions.json records only the manifest URL and sha256).
findings.required_fix: Update docs/CI.md to enumerate all four pinned actions with their reviewed tags and commits, including actions/setup-python@a26af69b and dtolnay/rust-toolchain@683b588c, and record the tag-to-commit verification for the two newly added pins (or state explicitly that dtolnay/rust-toolchain is pinned to an untagged commit and why). Add the matching inline version comment to the dtolnay `uses:` lines in .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml.

findings.description: Two further docs/CI.md statements are now false for the corrected workflow. Line 13-14 says "The workflow installs Rust 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 as needed, with rustfmt and Clippy; it does not change the runner's default toolchain", but the pinned action runs `rustup default "$toolchain" --force-non-host` (.local/ci-bootstrap-2026-10-17/rust-toolchain.action.yml:111-116), so the runner default is changed. Line 11 says the runner "must supply ... Python 3.11 or newer, rustup", which contradicts both the corrected workflow (setup-python and the rust-toolchain action now install them) and docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:199-201 ("Rust and Python need not be preinstalled"); it also contradicts the enforced pin, since tools/test_ci.py:84-87 requires >= 3.12 and .python-version is 3.14.7. Line 11 and line 79 also require CMake, which docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:16-17 states the selected transport configuration does not need.
findings.required_fix: Correct docs/CI.md lines 10-14 and 77-80 to state the actual runner prerequisites (Git, Node for JavaScript actions, Bash, HTTPS/curl, C/C++ toolchain), that Rust and Python are installed by the pinned actions, the enforced Python floor (3.12) and pin (3.14.7), that the pinned action does set the runner default toolchain while all project scripts select toolchains explicitly with `+version`, and reconcile the CMake requirement with docs/DEVELOPMENT.md.
